data.content: Using TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY relationships (`tox_value_mg_L`) and measured concentrations (MEASURED_AT), which substances have the smallest margin between measured levels and toxicity values (i.e., highest implied risk), and does this align with them being labeled drivers (IS_DRIVER)?

args.query: For species = algae (unicellular), compute Toxic Unit TU = median_concentration_mg_L / tox_value_mg_L for all substance–site–year–quarter combinations where median_concentration_mg_L > 0 and a TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY value exists. Return the top 15 rows with the highest TU. For each row include: substance_name, site_name, country (if available), year, quarter, median_concentration_mg_L, tox_value_mg_L, TU, and whether an IS_DRIVER relationship exists for that substance at that site and time point. Sort by TU descending.

For species = daphnia/crustaceans (invertebrates), compute Toxic Unit TU = median_concentration_mg_L / tox_value_mg_L for all substance–site–year–quarter combinations where median_concentration_mg_L > 0 and a TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY value exists. Return the top 15 rows with the highest TU. For each row include: substance_name, site_name, country (if available), year, quarter, median_concentration_mg_L, tox_value_mg_L, TU, and whether an IS_DRIVER relationship exists for that substance at that site and time point. Sort by TU descending.

For species = fish (vertebrates), compute Toxic Unit TU = median_concentration_mg_L / tox_value_mg_L for all substance–site–year–quarter combinations where median_concentration_mg_L > 0 and a TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY value exists. Return the top 15 rows with the highest TU. For each row include: substance_name, site_name, country (if available), year, quarter, median_concentration_mg_L, tox_value_mg_L, TU, and whether an IS_DRIVER relationship exists for that substance at that site and time point. Sort by TU descending.

EcoToxFred here. I computed Toxic Units (TU = median_concentration_mg_L / tox_value_mg_L) to find the smallest margin between measured levels and toxicity values (i.e., highest implied risk), and checked whether those cases are labeled as drivers (IS_DRIVER) for the same site, time, and species.

Top high-risk cases by species (highest TU first)
- Algae (unicellular)
  - Bifenox — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 62.68, driver: false
  - Diflufenican — site: skivarpsan (Sweden), 2012 Q4, TU ≈ 42.59, driver: true
  - Diflufenican — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 42.26, driver: false
  - Zinc — site: chambon ou rau de la touche a saintlin (France), 2018 Q3, TU ≈ 33.04, driver: true
  - Flufenacet — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 29.67, driver: false
  - Alignment among top 15: 10 of 15 are labeled drivers.

- Daphnia/crustaceans (invertebrates)
  - Deltamethrin — site: n34 (Sweden), 2009 Q3, TU ≈ 1283.09, driver: true
  - Deltamethrin — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 877.90, driver: false
  - tau-Fluvalinate — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 858.43, driver: false
  - Bifenthrin — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 677.44, driver: false
  - Cyfluthrin — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 626.20, driver: false
  - Alignment among top 15: 4 of 15 are labeled drivers (11 are not).

- Fish (vertebrates)
  - Procymidone — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 368.06, driver: false
  - Cyfluthrin — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 111.63, driver: false
  - Benz(a)anthracene — site: dunieres a dunieres (France), 2009 Q3, TU ≈ 66.39, driver: true
  - Benz(a)anthracene — site: loire a villerest (France), 2009 Q3, TU ≈ 61.95, driver: true
  - tau-Fluvalinate — site: 11wvo001 (Netherlands), 2011 Q4, TU ≈ 53.02, driver: false
  - Alignment among top 15: 8 of 15 are labeled drivers.

Overall takeaways (grounded in the retrieved data)
- The smallest margins (highest TUs) occur in crustaceans, led by Deltamethrin (TU up to ~1283), but many of these high-risk instances are not flagged as drivers.
- For algae and fish, a majority of the top high-TU instances are labeled drivers, indicating better alignment between high implied risk and driver designation in those groups.

OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[d:IS_DRIVER {species:'algae'}]->(l)
